CCB Standard Operating Procedure — Bug Ticketing Process

Objective

The Change Control Board (CCB) is an internal governance body responsible for overseeing and managing the resolution of tickets reported by the Customer Success (CS) team. It was established to bring structure, accountability, and predictability to the ticket resolution process — ensuring that issues are triaged, prioritised, and resolved in a consistent and timely manner. The long-term goal of the CCB is to systematically reduce the volume of incoming tickets by identifying recurring patterns, addressing root causes, and feeding insights back into the product roadmap.

This document outlines the standard operating procedure (SOP) for the CCB ticketing process. It covers:

  • SLAs for ticket response and resolution times
  • The ticket lifecycle, including stages and stage-wise ownership
  • Ticket fields, their definitions, and ownership
  • Required format for the ticket description
  • The escalation matrix

All stakeholders (CS & CCB members) involved in the ticketing workflow are required to follow this SOP.

Tenets (Unless you know better..)

  • Root cause over symptom: Where a fix can address the underlying cause, it should. A workaround that closes a ticket but leaves the problem intact is not a resolution.
  • Customer impact over internal convenience: When prioritising between tickets, the severity of customer impact takes precedence over what is technically easier or faster to resolve.
  • Impact defines severity, not urgency: A ticket is P0 because the defined criteria are met — not because it was escalated loudly. We classify based on evidence, not pressure.
  • Completeness before speed: A ticket worked on with incomplete information creates more rework than a ticket returned for clarity. We don't start what we can't finish well.
  • Defer with intent, not by default: Deferring a ticket is an active decision that requires explicit justification. Complexity alone is not a reason to defer — the effort must genuinely outweigh the impact.
  • Every issue is a product signal: Recurring bugs are not just tickets to close. They are inputs to the roadmap. The CCB is responsible for surfacing patterns, not just resolving individual tickets.
  • Ownership is clear at every stage: At any point in a ticket's lifecycle, exactly one person owns it. Ambiguity in ownership is the fastest way for a ticket to stall.

Section 1: SLAs for Ticket Resolution

Key Definitions

  • CCB Response Time: The duration between ticket creation and the first response from the CCB team. A first response takes one of two forms: assigning the ticket to a technical POC if all required information has been provided, or reverting it to the ticket raiser if information is incomplete (Refer Section 4 for the required ticket description format).
  • CCB Resolution Time: The duration between the date of assignment and the date on which the reported issue is resolved i.e., the fix is developed (may not be deployed yet) and verified as working by the QA.
  • CS Response time: The duration between the CCB reverting a ticket to the ticket raiser and CS providing the requested information. CS is expected to respond within 1 business day. If CS does not respond within this time, the ticket is downgraded to P3. If CS does not respond within a further 4 business days, the ticket is closed and a new ticket needs to be opened (no re-opening of old ticket).

P0 — Critical 1) System is down or core functionality is impacted for multiple users across one or more clients, with no workaround available. 2) System is down or core functionality is impacted for single user with no workaround available for a premium/critical client. 4–8 hours (within 1 business day) 1–2 business days Immediate hot fix release — same day or next day.
P1 — High 1) System is down or core functionality is impacted for single user, with no workaround available for a non-premium client. 2) System is down or core functionality is impacted for multiple users across one or more clients. Workaround exists but is highly non-scalable. 1–3 business days 1 week Prioritised in the current sprint; released at end-of-sprint or as a hot fix if end-of-sprint is not a release cycle — release decision to be mutually agreed upon by Engineering, Product, and CS.
P2 — Medium 1) A workaround exists but involves friction and is difficult to scale. 2–5 business days 2–4 weeks Addressed in the next 1–2 sprints and follows the sprint release cycle.
P3 — Low Cosmetic issues, minor bugs or feature enhancements, usage gaps due to incorrect CS training documentation. 5–8 business days Based on roadmap and other priorities —

Section 2: Ticket Lifecycle

The flowchart below illustrates the three primary ticket states — Open, Resolved, Closed — along with the sub-states within each and the team responsible at every stage.

State 1: Open

  • Unassigned: Default status when a ticket is raised.
  • More Info Required: Further information required from CS stakeholder to proceed with the ticket.
  • Assigned: A developer has been assigned but has not yet picked up the ticket.
  • In Progress: The developer has started working on the issue.
  • Product Feedback Required: Input is needed from the Product team to proceed.
  • Awaiting Code Review: Development is complete and the PR is awaiting code review.
  • Code review complete: Code review is complete, ready to be pushed into test environments.
  • Deferred: The ticket is not picked post assessment. This could be due to very large effort required vs the impact, or because it is an enhancement request that will be tracked in Canny. Requests in Canny will be picked by the sprint teams and not the support team.
  • Awaiting QA: The fix is developed and deployed in FIT/UAT and awaiting testing by the QA team.

State 2: Resolved

  • Awaiting deployment: QA has verified and provided sign off.
  • Business Review (or Prod Deployed): The fix has been deployed to production and is pending CS/Business review on production.
  • RCA pending: The fix has been deployed to production, however the RCA write-up is pending due to which the ticket cannot be closed.

State 3: Closed

  • Verified: Client has been informed of the fix and has not reported/come back with any issues. RCA is also closed.
  • Non-response: The ticket was closed by CCB team due to non-response from CS stakeholder.

3.3 Auto-Calculated fields

S.No.Field NameOwnerAcceptable Values
1Tech Response TimeAutoTime between ticket creation and the ticket first moved to Open: Assigned state.
2CS Response TimeAutoCumulative time where the ticket was pending on Open: More Info Requested. We record cumulative number for this state as there can be back & forth from Open: More Info Requested to Open: Assigned states.
3Resolution TimeAutoCumulative time where the ticket was pending on Tech team states (Open: Assigned to Open: Awaiting QA). We record cumulative number for this state as there can be back & forth from Open: More Info Requested to Open: Assigned states.
4CS Response StartAutoTimestamp gets recorded when ticket moved to Open: More Info Requested. The timestamp is reset every time the movement is made. This timestamp is used for CS Response Ageing Calculation.
5Resolution StartAutoTimestamp gets recorded when ticket moved to Open: Assigned state. The timestamp is reset every time the movement is made. This timestamp is used for Resolution Ageing Calculation.
6CS Response AgeingAutoCalculated for tickets which are in Open: More Info Requested state. It records the time between the 'CS Response Start' timestamp to the current timestamp.
7Tech Response AgeingAutoCalculated for tickets which are in Open: Unassigned state. It records the time between the ticket creation to the current timestamp.
8Resolution AgeingAutoCalculated for tickets which are in one of the pending on Tech team states (Open: Assigned to Open: Awaiting QA). It records the time between the 'Resolution Start' timestamp to current timestamp.
9Priority ChangeAutoUpdates the values to 'Upgraded', 'Downgraded', 'No change' basis the current vs initial priority assigned at the time of raising the ticket.
10Initial PriorityAutoRecords the initial priority given at the time of raising the ticket.

Section 4: Ticket Body Format

Every ticket must clearly address the following. If a section is not applicable, enter "NA."

  1. What steps will reproduce the problem?
  2. What is the expected outcome?
  3. What happens instead? Attach screenshots or screen recordings where possible.
  4. Have you identified any workarounds or temporary fixes? If yes, describe them.
  5. Have you tried refreshing the page, re-performing the action, or testing in an incognito window, a different browser, a different account, or a different system?

Below is a sample response of a good ticket:

Note: Any ticket that does not follow the above format will be reverted to "More Info Requested" status. The CS stakeholder will be required to provide the necessary information in the correct format before the ticket is processed further.

Section 5: Tech/PM Response Expectations

Tech/PM may respond to a ticket under one of two scenarios:

(a) More Info Requested

The ticket lacks sufficient detail for Tech/PM to assess or action it. The response must include:

  • The specific information requested from the CS team
  • Why this information is needed (i.e., what it will be used to determine)

(b) Ticket Marked Invalid

The ticket is a non-issue or reflects expected platform behavior. The response must include:

  • The reason the ticket is invalid (e.g., working as designed, duplicate, out of scope)
  • The workaround or resolution the CS team can share with the customer

Note: In both scenarios, use @mention when replying so the CS team is notified.

CS Training Notes

Once formula configuration for cashless is done, the Cashless payment mode can be enabled/disabled through Admin panel. Check for admin panel & cashless flag in issuer listing page prior to raising cashless activation issue related tickets.
While updating FMV by grant, choose Add & Update action appropriately. Add must be chosen when there is no previous FMV present & Update when a previous FMV is present.
Getting a list of all stakeholders with Aadhaar documents attached is possible in the platform by selecting: Stakeholders -> Stakeholder Details -> Actions -> Download -> Aadhaar Documents.
Whenever we observe system discrepancies such as option movement not happening as per separation rules, unable to process exercise due to validation errors, award units reflecting in one area & not in another screen/area, CS is advised to check for award inconsistencies (any grant report) & try to resolve the same manually, prior to raising a ticket.
Unable to make payment: if the stakeholder is added under 'Resident' and there is no entry for scope 'Resident' in payments (payment configuration is only set for Company level), add the payment method at Resident level too, in Exercise Configuration -> Payment Configurations.
Exercise form details can be edited by using the Reinstate option for exercises where Payment is not approved. Post re-instatement, the Admin can edit the information and regenerate the exercise forms.
403 error: this error is not related to the platform. It is an internet accessibility related issue which needs to be resolved from the client's IT team.
EULA not being accepted may happen due to the client's system, firewall, or VPN. CS may ask the user to try with their personal laptop to check, prior to raising a ticket.
If a request from the user's browser to the S3 domain is blocked on the client's own network (firewalls, corporate proxies, or DNS/allow-lists rejecting outbound traffic), the PDF viewer shows a generic load-failure message ('invalid URL or access restrictions'). The URL itself is not invalid - the connection is being blocked. Ask the client to whitelist the AWS S3 URL.
If the valuation formula configuration is set to 'TransactionDate-1' (FMV value from the previous day), the status may not show as 'Awaiting FMV' but something else (e.g. 'Awaiting Payment Details' or 'Pending Sale Initiation'). CS should check the formula configuration before raising tickets on incorrect exercise statuses.
If an employee-level tax rate is configured, it takes the highest precedence; if not configured, the system falls back to country-level tax rates. Check if employee tax rates are configured correctly before raising a tech ticket.
If a client requires exercising in decimals, check whether the 'exercise in decimal units' config is enabled from the exercise configuration page before raising a ticket.
A common troubleshooting step when the Net Banking payment option is not showing during the exercise step is to refresh the browser, clear the cache, and try again.
Audit log feature is added in the issuer listing page. This feature needs to be explored prior to raising any Audit log related requests.
Double check the formula configuration before raising a support ticket on configuration - mistakes in formula input have caused process breaks.
CS needs to provide the right formula configuration.
Tax rates can be edited from the frontend - CS team should check before raising a ticket.
PII data is not to be attached in tickets.
If 'capture separate payment details exercise and tax amount' is not enabled, but the Settlement transaction on UI was updated with both payment details via backend, reports will not show the payment details. Enable the 'capture separate payment details exercise and tax amount' configuration to have the details show on reports.
Attach the approval email from Amit on issuer deletion before raising a ticket for deletion.
Rounding off for Perquisite value for exercises can be done using the edit configuration for an instrument in the instrument types page.
Settlement transaction values cannot be updated once the state is moved to 'Shares Issued'. The only method is to delete and re-record the settlement transaction.
There is no auto-disapproval for the fund partner (Funding) payment method.
Notification template configuration is needed to enable the email notification for Fund partner disbursement request rejection. Check if this is present prior to raising tickets on notifications being absent for this use case.
For HRMS data issues, check if the field names & mappings are correct prior to raising tickets.
A grant summary report showing tranches is not an issue - the report configuration for the summary report shows as per customization.
The New Employee Dashboard flag has to be enabled to see dashboards for instruments that are not predefined in the system, like RSU.
If NetPayout amounts are showing incorrect, check the configured formula.
If an employee is facing login issues, check if the employee has multiple email ids associated with the issuer. Ask the employee to logout and login using the right employee id.
An exercise request summary email trigger to the CR/Admin can be set up via the new notifications configuration.
To change the grant value (basis funding rounds) on the employee dashboard, use the valuation configuration dashboard.
If an employee or stakeholder from the issuer is not receiving an email, one potential reason is that their email could be part of the AWS suppression list (sent by DevOps). Confirm this before raising a ticket.
All documents associated with a stakeholder are downloadable via UI: go to stakeholder page -> Actions -> Download -> and choose the documents needed.
All feature flags can be enabled or disabled through the issuers-listing page.
If one of the CRs/Admins has another employee's name displayed, update the required details either by changing the user's access and updating the email, or by de-associating the user and recreating the link. Once a user is linked to an email, their details cannot be modified directly in the system.
Bulk upload for settlement of Custom Instruments and SARs is now possible on the platform.
Exercise Form: if the «System Date» token is used in the exercise form template, the date shows in UTC. If the user needs the date in the issuer's time zone, use the «Exercise Date» token instead.
If grants are of type 'click to accept/click to approve' and not E-Sign grants, then E-Sign will not be reflected.
Reinstating to a previous step is not possible in the old settlement (exercise) workflow.
When we change the email id for any stakeholder, it sends all pending user task mails to the new email id.
Check if the payment method token has been added in the exercise form if payment method is not getting captured in the exercise form.
If an exercise was created by the employee before a quick note update, by design the previous quick note is displayed to the employee. Quick notes do not change on existing transactions when the instrument config is later updated.
The number of decimals for the FMV value shown in the exercise window is driven by Instrument configuration. To change the decimals, use the instrument configuration.
Reinstating the exercise is not needed in order to regenerate the form.
If the data room is zoomed in (e.g. 150%), the 'New file' button may not be visible. The user needs to zoom out.
Avoid including sensitive information like API keys or passwords directly in a YouTrack ticket. Share those details with the assigned developer via an encrypted file instead.
If the Stakeholder is missing the ResidentStatus custom field value in stakeholder details, updating payment modes will skip the exercise since there is no value for resident.
Exercise Ids need to always be sequential. If validation fails for an exercise, the generated ID may be skipped; the next successful attempt gets the next id in sequence. Users may feel ids are missing, but this might not be the case.
Exercises will fail if mandatory required stakeholder details are not filled in - for example, if nominee is mandatory and not provided, the exercise will not go through.
Configuration for user invite email is needed so that email is sent to user
Tax rate configuration alone is not sufficient. There needs to be Tax identifier country updated at the stakeholder level and mobility as well uploaded via bulk upload (in case it mobility is switched on)
Your Equity Awards widget takes (Vested and Available + Unvested) as a unit for calculations. It is common mistake to assume it takes all granted. But that is not the case. 
Different paraters can sometimes have different currencies in the platform. Not taking care of the currency conversion and doing the calculations can lead to incorrect numbers. For example, if FMV is in USD and exercise price is in CAD, subtracting these will give wrong spread. 
Triggers and configuration pre-requisites are needed for emails. Please check if them before raising a ticket for emails not being sent by system. Examples - 1) "Acknowledgement: Options Exercise Process completed" email only gets triggered if the exercise is actually completed. 2) The Payment confirmation mail needs the toggle "Notify Grantees regarding payment confirmation" to be turned on. 3) The configuration for user invite email had been disabled so email was not sent
It is recommended to wait for 1 day before raising tickets for payment processing (stuck) cases. 
The transfer to personal email flag in the stakeholder separation configurations settings needs to be enabled before separating the employee, if the issuer wants the transfer to happen.
CS needs to check if the stakeholder's email is updated before raising ticket for stakeholder not receiving notifications
The visibility of tax being displayed on exercise can be controlled from instrument configuration. There is an option of display (yes/ No)
CS needs to wait for 1 day before raising tickets on HRIS sync details not showing up on the HRIS update email
The current value of equity awards in the employee dashboard is driven by the valuation we ask the system to pick in the dashboard valuation configuration section. If the configuration is FMV and say the FMV expires, then the system falls back to zero instead of showing stale value. Thus CS needs to ensure correct configuration and check availability of the configured valuation. 
IDP service is common across all servers. If an email is used for issuers across one server and same email is used for another server- there will not be any first time user login email triggered by our system. 
When email change is done with E-sign flow and the grant letter is not yet signed, it is expected for the grant to be reinitiated as the grant letter needs to be generated again with the new email. This happens for cases where separation events occur.
Detailed captable access for users is required for them to be able to download the captable reports from the reports section
Client can sometimes configure incorrect API key. This can lead to failed HRIS sync. 
When client as different expiry date for each trache (Expire post XX period from vest date), then the reports will show "As defined in the Plan / Scheme Document" rather than showing the actual expiry date for grant. This is because there are multiple expiry dates for each tranche. 
Check the employee id, email stakeholder id as well insted of relying on just name, before arriving at conclusion that certain grants are not reflecting for certain employees. There can be cases where 2 employees has same name- which is why some grants may not be visible against one of the names (they are under the other name)
In case any stakeholder or employee has 2 logins to Qapita, they need to ensure they are using the right login before confirming that they are seeing the wrong data/dashboard.
New exercise flow can be enabled from the issuer listing page.
